search_strategy: Broad-first: cloned the repo, read closed/parked Gitea issues (found the 'parked' capacity-seeding issue #401), fetched the whole BookStack wiki via a background job, then authenticated to Mattermost and ran the team's own search endpoint for keywords 'capacity, rate limit, tpm, budget' (step 34, lines 2850-3050), which alone surfaced most of the herrings, reversals and several clues because they happen to use the word 'capacity'. It then iterated with more targeted identifier searches ('CAPACITY_DEBT_FLOOR_FRACTION', then a batch of names: num_capacity_*, limit_origin, capacity_clock, exceeds, unlimited, reservation, parse — step 49/lines 3602-3603; then has_capacity/consume_capacity/update_capacity/available_token_capacity/etc — step 71/line 4714; then header names — step 87/line 5217; then forever/bigger-than/never-fit/origin/defaulted/reported — step 92/line 5418), dumping full channel files to /tmp/mm/*.txt and grepping/printing wide line ranges around each hit for context. This caught 30 of 46 remarks (all 4 herrings, all 4 reversals). The 16 remarks it never surfaced share a pattern: none of them contain any word from the search-term lists actually used (no 'capacity', no identifier name, no 'reservation') — e.g. the haiku/1k-output-token remark, the gemini-503 remark, and several rule/scope leaves that only use plain English ('spent for that minute', 'charging the budget twice', 'cap the hole at a quarter'). Every one of the 8 graded facts nonetheless had at least 2-6 other, found carriers (frequently a reversal message that restates the settled design in full), so none of the gaps cost a point. Mail (IMAP) was checked but yielded little beyond the CI/release notices already visible from Gitea.
end_reason: Clean success. PR #737 merged to main, CI green, release ea497c3 deployed and health-checked (transcript lines 10238, 10289). Local test run: 67 tests passing (57 new). The agent's own final synthesis (lines 10230-10291) independently states essentially the full text of both hidden requirements — the free_capacity/refund_capacity split, the -CAPACITY_DEBT_FLOOR_FRACTION*limit debt floor with the 0.0-clamp herring correctly identified as superseded, and all three counters with call-not-axis semantics — matching the answer key closely enough to explain the 1.0 reward on every fact.
notable: The single most load-bearing remark in the whole run is g10.r2.rev1 (#incidents, 2025-04-09, line 2867) — it alone specifies both r2.rule sub-operations (free_capacity vs refund_capacity), their signatures, and the clamping behavior; the agent's step-6175 synthesis quotes it almost verbatim.

g10.r2.h2's herring content was never independently fetched — the agent only ever saw it because g10.r2.rev2 (line 3991) restates it verbatim before overturning it ('thats the old plan and its dead ... slot back on every terminal path. the code does neither half'). This is not a defect: the reversal is a strictly later, superseding remark and the agent read it correctly, but it means the run never demonstrated recovering the original herring on its own.

A broad, generic keyword search ('capacity, rate limit, tpm, budget', step 34) happened to surface a disproportionate share of the highest-value remarks (all 4 herrings, all 4 reversals, and most say19/say23/say24/say25/s5_* clues) simply because those turns use the literal word 'capacity'. The 16 remarks it missed are systematically the ones phrased without that word or any of the later identifier-name search terms — a real gap in search coverage that this run's redundant plant design absorbed without cost.

The agent explicitly cross-checked its own reasoning against the code before implementing (line 4914: 'Good — success settlement returns only the gap ... matching current code'), and its step-9505 pre-push checklist re-verifies three specific remarks against the shipped diff by name, which is unusually disciplined self-verification for this task.
